title: Selection, Coverage & Nonresponse Bias
interviewAnswer: More data does not fix a systematically unrepresentative sample. Selection and nonresponse bias occur when inclusion/response is related to the outcome or variables of interest.
keyPoints: Distinguish sampling variance from systematic bias.
Weighting can help only when selection is modeled with adequate information.
Instrumentation and eligibility define the population actually observed.
why: Selection, Coverage & Nonresponse Bias is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
intuition: Distinguish sampling variance from systematic bias.
deepDive: More data does not fix a systematically unrepresentative sample. Selection and nonresponse bias occur when inclusion/response is related to the outcome or variables of interest. Weighting can help only when selection is modeled with adequate information. Instrumentation and eligibility define the population actually observed. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: An opt-in survey of power users can produce extremely precise but biased estimates of overall satisfaction.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Selection, Coverage & Nonresponse Bias?
How would you validate or tune Selection, Coverage & Nonresponse Bias?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
